hero.title: I build AI systems that *hold up* in production.
hero.subtitle: AI engineer and published researcher based in Islamabad. Three and a half years shipping agentic systems, RAG pipelines and document AI for real business workflows — and, at NUST's MachVis Lab, vision-language models for radiology.

about.title: An engineer with a *researcher's* habits.
about.description: I ship LLM systems for production teams, and I study how multimodal models can be grounded, efficient and trustworthy.
paragraphs: For about three and a half years I've been delivering end-to-end AI systems — multi-agent LangGraph backends, hybrid retrieval, evaluation pipelines and computer-vision document extraction — for teams in the US, Australia and Pakistan, from early-stage startups to Oracle enterprise clients.

In parallel, I do research on multimodal and vision-language models for 2D and 3D medical imaging. At the MachVis Lab at NUST I co-developed Radixpert, an anatomy-guided model for radiology report generation published at IEEE, and FeLoRA16-SPP, a parameter-efficient 3D multimodal LLM for the MICCAI 2025 FLARE challenge.

Both sides feed each other: research taught me to measure before I claim, and production taught me what actually survives contact with real users. I write about applied AI on Medium and publish open models and datasets on Hugging Face.

research.title: Making medical AI *grounded* and efficient.
research.description: My research is on multimodal and vision-language models for 2D and 3D medical imaging — teaching models to look at the right anatomy, and adapting large foundation models without retraining them.
interests: Reliable RAG & agentic LLM systems and their evaluation

publications.title: Radixpert: A Multimodal Approach to Medical Imaging
publications.summary: A dual-branch vision-language model that fuses frozen BioViL image features with anatomical segmentation masks from a frozen U-Net to condition MedGemma-4B for chest X-ray report generation. LoRA trains ~1.8% of parameters on 16,000 PadChest studies; explicit anatomical grounding reduced laterality errors.

result.label: RadCliQ — on par with the strongest baseline (Reg2RG, 0.810)

publications.title: FeLoRA16-SPP: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of 3D Multimodal LLMs for Radiology Report Generation and Visual Question Answering
publications.summary: Adapts the M3D-LaMed 3D multimodal LLM to report generation and VQA on 3D CT scans, combining LoRA fine-tuning with a spatial pooling projector and a frozen vision encoder — about 8% of 4.07B parameters trainable. Top scores on 9 of 18 organ systems.

result.label: Average GREEN score — up to 12% above PHI3, 4% above Med3DVLM
